content: Chevron Corporation CVX is slated to release third-quarter 2026 results on Oct. 30, before market open. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for revenues is pegged at $60.5 billion, implying an increase of 21.6% from the year-ago quarter. The consensus earnings mark of $4.78 per share has been revised upward by 0.8% over the past seven days, suggesting a 158.4% jump from the year-ago reported number. For full-year 2026, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for CVX’s revenues is pegged at $240.9 billion, implying an improvement of 27.5% year over year. The consensus mark for 2026 earnings per share is $18.20, indicating a surge of 149.7%. In the last reported quarter, the company delivered an earnings surprise of 4.5%. Chevron’s earnings beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate in each of the trailing four quarters, with the average surprise being 18.7%. Chevron’s downstream operations are likely to have benefited from favorable refining margins and its flexible refining network during the third quarter of 2026. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for total downstream earnings is $5.1 billion, higher than $1.1 billion reported in the year-ago quarter. Chevron’s integrated refining and marketing operations, diverse crude-processing capabilities and ability to maintain high utilization amid market disruptions could have supported profitability. However, management projected third-quarter turnaround and downtime expenses of $175-$225 million, which may have partially offset these benefits. Chevron’s growing production base, supported by Hess assets, the Permian Basin and Kazakhstan’s Tengiz operations, could have strengthened third-quarter upstream performance. Management projected full-year 2026 production of 3.98-4.10 million barrels of oil equivalent per day, representing 7-10% growth excluding asset sales. At Tengiz, optimization increased the Third Generation Plant’s oil-processing capacity from 260,000 to 320,000 barrels daily, potentially supporting higher output. Meanwhile, the company’s $1.5 billion in Hess synergies, captured six months ahead of schedule, could have improved operating efficiency and supported profitability. Chevron’s companywide cost-saving measures are likely to have strengthened third-quarter profitability by reducing its operating expense burden. The company achieved $3 billion in annualized structural cost reductions during the 12 months ended June 2026, reaching its target six months earlier than planned. More than 70% of those savings came from efficiency improvements, including organizational restructuring, technology deployment, predictive maintenance and better turnaround planning. These measures could have helped Chevron absorb inflationary pressures while maintaining operational reliability. Improved cost efficiency may also have supported margins despite fluctuations in commodity prices. Rival ExxonMobil HoldingsXOM heads into its third-quarter earnings with stronger refining margins expected to drive results. The company estimates that improved refining margins could boost downstream earnings by approximately $4.5 billion sequentially, reflecting favorable fuel market conditions amid geopolitical supply disruptions. However, weaker crude prices are anticipated to reduce upstream earnings by roughly $1.3 billion from the preceding quarter. Additionally, unfavorable timing effects of approximately $2.5 billion could weigh on overall profitability. Gains of around $700 million from upstream asset divestments are expected to partially offset these headwinds, supporting ExxonMobil's quarterly performance. Meanwhile, European oil major Shell plcSHEL anticipates a stronger third-quarter 2026 performance, supported by record indicative refining margins of $42 per barrel, up from $24 in the preceding quarter. Integrated Gas production is projected at 740,000-780,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, benefiting from the ARC Resources acquisition. Trading performance is expected to remain stable, further supporting earnings prospects. However, lower LNG liquefaction volumes, weaker chemicals margins and reduced refinery utilization could partially offset these gains. Additionally, approximately $2.5 billion in German emissions-certificate payments and exploration write-offs may weigh on cash flows and reported profitability, respectively. Shares of Chevron have gone up 23.7% in the past three months compared with the broader Zacks Energy sector’s growth of 13.2%. Shares of XOM have gained 20.6%, while SHEL stock has gone up 24%. From a valuation perspective — in terms of forward price-to-earnings ratio — Chevron is trading at a premium compared to the industry average. The stock is also trading above its five-year mean of 11.81. Chevron appears well-positioned ahead of its third-quarter earnings release, supported by improving refining margins, expanding upstream production and sustained cost efficiencies. The company’s impressive earnings surprise history, upward estimate revisions and positive Earnings ESP strengthen expectations for another quarterly beat. Moreover, Hess-related synergies and operational improvements could support profitability. Although the stock’s premium valuation and recent rally warrant consideration, Chevron’s strong operational momentum and encouraging earnings outlook justify investor optimism. With the consensus projecting substantial year-over-year earnings growth, investors may consider adding CVX to their portfolios ahead of the upcoming results, despite near-term uncertainties. Chevron Corporation CVX has made further progress in assessing its offshore natural gas opportunity in Egypt after the Nargis-2 well delivered positive drilling results in the Mediterranean Sea. In an Oct. 24 announcement, Egypt's Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources said the well confirmed the continuation of gas-bearing reservoirs identified earlier and encountered another gas-bearing interval. The results give Chevron and its partners more information for evaluating the discovery, but additional work is required before a commercial development decision can be made. Nargis-2 was drilled to a depth of more than 5,000 meters, and technical evaluation found net gas pay of up to 35 meters. The well also tested deeper geological layers, including formations associated with high pressure and temperature. Together, these findings help geologists build a clearer picture of the subsurface and assess whether the gas-bearing zones can support a viable project. However, the reported thickness is not a measure of total gas reserves, and it does not establish how much gas could ultimately be recovered. Drilling began in May 2026, with Chevron working alongside its partners and the Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Company ("EGAS"). The well was planned to investigate the extent of the Nargis discovery and test additional formations below the intervals previously encountered. The presence of another gas-bearing layer is an encouraging result because it adds to the geological information available for the next stage of appraisal. The latest update does not provide a revised estimate of the field's resources or confirm a development schedule. Chevron and its partners will need to interpret the well data, assess reservoir characteristics and determine the technical and financial requirements of a potential development. Such work is especially important for offshore projects, where drilling, subsea facilities and supporting infrastructure can require significant investment. Until the appraisal results are translated into a development plan, the timing and scale of future production remain uncertain. Chevron operates the Nargis area with Eni, Mubadala Energy and Egypt's Tharwa Petroleum. The current contractor interests are 45% for Chevron, 30% for Eni through its subsidiary IEOC, 15% for Mubadala Energy and 10% for Tharwa Petroleum. The contractor group works with EGAS, which holds a 50% share in the concession structure. The ownership mix gives Chevron an operating role in evaluating the discovery while spreading participation across several energy companies. Mubadala Energy completed its acquisition of a 15% interest from Eni in February 2026, leaving it with a 30% contractor interest. The companies will need to coordinate technical studies and future investment decisions as the project moves through appraisal. The partners' participation is not, on its own, evidence that a final investment decision has been made. Egypt's petroleum ministry has identified the development of previously discovered but undeveloped resources as a priority. The policy aims to encourage exploration partners to continue investing and to move discoveries toward recoverable reserves and eventual production. If Nargis proves commercially viable, it could contribute to domestic natural gas supply and support Egypt's broader efforts to develop offshore resources. For Egypt, the key question is whether the field can be developed at a cost and pace that make sense under prevailing market conditions. More domestic gas production could provide an additional supply source, but that outcome depends on the volume of recoverable gas, the infrastructure required and the time needed to bring the asset online. The latest well results are a step in that process, not a guarantee of future output. For Chevron investors, Nargis-2 adds a potential long-term growth opportunity to its international portfolio. A successful project could eventually contribute to production, but the announcement does not quantify the impact on Chevron's earnings, cash flow or capital spending. It would therefore be premature to treat the drilling results as an immediate financial catalyst. The next developments to watch are an updated assessment of the discovery, details on recoverable resources, the proposed development approach and any timeline for commercial production. Investors should also look for clarity on expected capital requirements and project economics. These factors will help establish whether the discovery can progress from geological promise to a project that creates value for Chevron and its partners. Overall, Nargis-2 has delivered encouraging evidence that the known gas-bearing formations extend further and that an additional interval may be worth evaluating. The findings strengthen the case for continued appraisal, while leaving the field's commercial scale and development prospects open. For now, Chevron has more data to work with; a clearer view of the asset's value will depend on the technical and commercial conclusions that follow. title: Why Did XOM, COP, CVX Jump To 52-Week Highs Last Week? - Stocktwits
content: Shares of energy companies Exxon Mobil Corp. (XOM), ConocoPhillips (COP) and Chevron Corp. (CVX) surged to annual highs on Friday as oil prices rallied to a six-month high amid growing geopolitical tensions. Brent crude futures maturing in December climbed over $116 per barrel on Friday, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures for December rose to $102.40 per barrel. Last week, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia intensified, stoking fears about energy security and infrastructure and shipments across the Middle East. Saudi Aramco evacuated its Dhahran headquarters after attacks in the country's eastern oil-producing region. While U.S. President Donald Trump said last week that Washington would not be negotiating with Tehran and suggested further developments could follow soon, on Sunday, he ruled out an attack on Iran this week. Meanwhile, though oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have recovered toward pre-war levels in recent weeks, with the U.S. Central Command aiding passage through the critical waterways, Citigroup analysts have warned that the recent improvement in shipments may not represent a sustained recovery. UBS analyst Giovanni Staunovo also reportedly told Reuters that any further escalation could trigger renewed supply disruptions. Brett Erickson, Managing Principal at Obsidian Risk Advisors, said in a post on X over the weekend, “Iran is currently launching missiles and drones at vessels attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz. Despite the preparations from all sides to ready for a full-scale resumption of the war, Iran does not intend to allow the U.S. to use this window to flow out excessive amount of oil and refined products in the meantime.” Exxon Mobil, ConocoPhillips and Chevron surged to 52-week highs on Friday amid the steep climb in oil prices. XOM stock hit a 52-week high of $183.75 during trading hours on Friday, closing nearly 3% higher. COP stock rallied to a 52-week high of $152.77 during regular trading, and ended 3.5% higher at close. CVX stock surged to a 52-week high of $ 233.74, closing up nearly 3%. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around XOM and CVX stocks was ‘bullish’ at the time of writing, while it was ‘bearish’ for COP. XOM stock has gained more than 49% year-to-date, while COP and CVX stocks have surged nearly 56% and 50%, respectively. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Shares of AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) slipped 0.4% overnight late Sunday even as the company sought more spectrum to expand its satellite broadband capabilities, while market veteran Herb Greenberg questioned its valuation despite a steep selloff. ASTS stock jumped nearly 3% on Friday to close at $39.70, but ended the week down 2%, marking its fourth consecutive weekly decline. In a Friday statement, AST’s unit, AST & Science, proposed adding Q/V and E-band service-link capabilities to its 248-satellite network. The links would connect satellites directly to customer terminals, broadening its proposed high-frequency operations beyond ground-gateway connections. The request covers selected frequencies between 40 and 51.4 GHz, plus downlinks at 71 GHz -74 GHz and uplinks at 81GHz –84 GHz.  “This supports a deployment model in which the smallest terminal classes can be used by functional mobile user equipment with varying bandwidths, powers, and antenna sizes,” AST said. The proposed services would require compatible terminals alongside AST’s core connectivity offering for standard smartphones. “AST SpaceMobile’s operations are not solely dependent on use of the E-band; AST SpaceMobile will utilize other spectrum, including the Q/V-band and 700/800 MHz bands, for its user terminals in addition to the E-band spectrum,” the filing said. Approval and interference coordination are still necessary, including protections for military users in certain bands. Meanwhile, Greenberg, a veteran financial journalist and investment researcher, questioned AST’s realistic profit potential despite its expanding addressable market. He noted that shares had lost over half their value over six months and recently hit a 52-week low. “Even with that, it’s still priced as if it’s the hottest thing ever, especially when compared with its more established Satcom peers,” he said. Greenberg highlighted an enterprise valuation of 140 times trailing revenue, versus 38 times for Globalstar, 7.5 times for Iridium and three times for Viasat. He also noted a trailing EBITDA loss of about $532 million. “Drilling deeper, based on trailing multiples, you wouldn’t know that its network is nowhere near fully built out yet,” he said. He highlighted multiples of 16 times estimated 2028 revenue and 324 times estimated 2028 adjusted EBITDA, based on $1 billion in revenue and $50 million in adjusted EBITDA. Greenberg acknowledged that a “sky-high valuation” alone rarely justifies avoiding or shorting a stock, while highlighting high short interest and Fidelity’s warning of securities-lending stress. AST is targeting initial, intermittent coverage before year-end in the United States, Canada, Japan, the United Kingdom and Saudi Arabia, subject to regulatory approvals. Continuous service will require more satellites. “We are moving toward service with the partnerships, spectrum and network capabilities needed to bring cellular broadband from space into people’s everyday lives,” President Scott Wisniewski said. The company has more than 60 gateways deployed, installed or planned, supporting over 60 mobile operators whose networks reach more than three billion subscribers. It targets 100 MHz of U.S. spectrum access and 5,600 activated coverage cells before year-end, up from over 3,000. Meanwhile, its smartphone-focused network has shown peak downloads of 98.9 Mbps, with next-gen satellites expected to reach about 200 Mbps. In Europe, Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefonica and Vodafone are exploring a joint mobile-satellite spectrum bid, with a satellite provider yet to be selected. On the other hand, Viasat has challenged an earlier AST overseas-spectrum application as “fatally flawed” over interference and allocation concerns. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for ASTS slipped to ‘neutral’ from ‘bullish’ levels a week ago amid a 29% decline in 24-hour message volumes. One user noted the fresh filing and said, “If I'm reading this right and it's correct, the SEC just gave ASTS the rights to compete with Starlink, reversing the competition for home broadband.” Lungisani Mhlongo on X (formerly Twitter): "A MAJOR TURNING POINT AWAITS $ASTS NEXT WEEK:Following Friday's market close, an SEC filing has fundamentally altered the landscape for $ASTS. Previously, the market viewed AST SpaceMobile merely as a backup ... Another user said, “Ast will be able to go after starlinks main business! I did not see this coming the TAM here just got a lot bigger!” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. SK Hynix (SKHY) is considering a special dividend of 16 trillion won ($12 billion), funded by gains from its investment in Japanese memory-chip maker Kioxia Holdings, South Korea’s Dong-A Ilbo reported Monday, citing unnamed investment banking sources. The payout would amount to about 80% of an estimated 20 trillion won in gains SK Hynix booked from its Kioxia investment in the first half of 2026. The company is expected to announce its plans alongside third-quarter earnings on Wednesday, according to the report. SK Hynix’s Seoul-listed shares rose marginally in Asian trading hours on Monday morning, while the U.S.-listed stock was up over 1% in overnight trading late Sunday. SK Hynix said it was reviewing options to return money to shareholders but had not decided on a special dividend, according to a Bloomberg report, which added that the prospect of a payout has helped the stock hold up amid a broader selloff in AI-related shares. SK Hynix joined a Bain Capital-led consortium in 2018 to acquire Toshiba’s former memory-chip business for $18 billion. Kioxia’s value climbed following its Tokyo stock-market debut in 2024. While Bain Capital sold its entire stake earlier this year, SK Hynix still holds convertible bonds linked to an investment vehicle with about a 14% stake in Kioxia, according to Bloomberg. Last week, SK Hynix scrapped plans for a U.S. IPO of its Solidigm flash-memory subsidiary. In an Oct. 23 statement, the South Korean chipmaker cited capital-market conditions and share-price trends behind its move. The IPO had reportedly targeted a $10 billion to $15 billion raise and a valuation of up to $150 billion. The decision follows a sharp correction in U.S. and South Korean semiconductor stocks. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for SKHY dipped over the past week but was ‘bullish’ as of late Sunday. “$SKHY Anyone who managed to top up like myself last week congratulations. We all got it at bargain basement prices,” a trader said. Another wrote: “Yes. And they are announcing another buyback next week. $SKHY is reducing its share float by about 3% per quarter. That's better than Apple. 200 fast. 300 in 2027.” SKHY stock closed at $137.02 on Friday and remains 8% below its Nasdaq listing price. Beyond SK Hynix’s report, investors will look at quarterly reports from Seagate Technology (STX) on Tuesday and Samsung Electronics on Thursday for fresh clues on the memory market. Additionally, the U.S. Central Command said on X that the commander of CENTCOM, Brad Cooper, visited the Strait of Hormuz on Oct. 25, as U.S. forces have helped Gulf partners export more than 1.5 billion barrels of crude oil since summer. CENTCOM also said it had helped more than 3,000 commercial vessels successfully transit the Strait over the last six months. "Today, primary transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz remain free and clear of Iranian sea mines thanks to incredible efforts by our people," said Cooper. "We remain intensely focused on keeping commercial traffic flowing as we work with our teammates in the U.S. interagency, Gulf Cooperation Council, and shipping industry." Oil prices pulled back from six-month highs overnight. Brent crude futures were trading at $114.85 a barrel, down 1.60%, while WTI crude futures traded nearly 2% lower at $101.28 per barrel. Meanwhile, as election season takes off worldwide, Trump reaffirmed his endorsement of Benjamin Netanyahu in the lead-up to the Israeli elections. “To the people of Israel, to those who haven’t seen it, I am attaching the Endorsement I gave one week ago to your Prime Minister, Bibi Netanyahu,” he said in a post on Truth Social. In Brazil, leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva defeated right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in a surprising turn of events, sending Brazilian stocks lower. Markets will now brace for a busy earnings week, with Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL), Microsoft Corporation (MSFT), and Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) set to report their earnings.
